options.text: The bending of waves as they pass from one medium to another
The bouncing of waves off a surface
The absorption of waves by a material
The spreading out of waves when they pass through a gap or around an obstacle

questions.explanation: Diffraction is the spreading out of waves when they pass through a gap or around an obstacle. It occurs with all types of waves.

questions.stem: Maximum diffraction occurs when the gap width is:
questions.explanation: Maximum diffraction occurs when the gap width is approximately equal to the wavelength of the wave. This produces significant spreading of the wave.

questions.stem: When a wave passes through a gap much larger than its wavelength:

options.text: The wave passes through with very little spreading

questions.explanation: When the gap is much larger than the wavelength, the wave passes through mostly unchanged with very little spreading at the edges.

questions.stem: Why can you hear someone talking around a corner but not see them?

options.text: Light is absorbed by walls but sound is not
Sound waves have longer wavelengths that diffract around corners; light wavelengths are too small
Sound can reflect but light cannot

questions.explanation: Sound waves have wavelengths (about 0.02-17 m) comparable to doorway sizes, so they diffract significantly. Visible light has tiny wavelengths (about 400-700 nm), so it hardly diffracts around everyday objects.

options.text: Speed, frequency, or wavelength of the wave

questions.explanation: Diffraction changes the direction and shape of wavefronts but does not change the speed, frequency, or wavelength of the wave.

questions.stem: Radio waves can be received behind hills because:

options.text: Their long wavelengths allow them to diffract around hills
They are reflected by the atmosphere only

questions.explanation: Radio waves have long wavelengths (metres or more), comparable to the size of hills, so they diffract significantly around these obstacles.

questions.stem: As a gap becomes narrower (closer to the wavelength), the amount of diffraction:
questions.explanation: As the gap narrows and approaches the wavelength, diffraction increases. The wave spreads out more and more into the region beyond the gap.
